2026-05-14_164438.webp.description: Day 1 of the trip, reached Ya'an after a 130km ride from Chengdu.

2026-05-15_182949.webp.description: An obelisk in Xingou, a small village in the mountains where I stayed overnight. The owner of the hostel has a reputation of being a good cook among the cyclists.

2026-05-16_121256.webp.description: After the tunnel of Erlangshan, the snow peaks are now visible in the distance.

2026-05-16_190204.webp.description: Luding Bridge over the Dadu River, a significant historical site from the Long March of the Red Army. Behind it is the newly built expressway bridge.

2026-05-17_135649.webp.description: Looking back before the tunnel. Road signs warning of slippery conditions, continuous downhill (which I just climbed up), and high traffic accident risk.

2026-05-17_210400.webp.description: Kangding city at night, known for traditional folk songs.

2026-05-19_112630.webp.description: Winding snowy roads going up to the Zheduo Mountain pass, the first high pass of G318 at 4298m. It was said that if one can cycle up to this pass, they would be set to finish the entire G318 journey (not true).

2026-05-19_162900.webp.description: Going downslope from Zheduo Mountain. I got a bad muscle injury after this ride, and could barely walk at the same night.

2026-05-21_155537.webp.description: Local legend says that when Princess Wencheng was traveling to Tibet, the life-sized statue of a 12-year-old Sakyamuni Buddha she was carrying miraculously became immovable here until a replica was left behind in this temple. Tibetans believe that if you cannot make the pilgrimage all the way to Lhasa, worshipping at Tagong Monastery yields the exact same spiritual merit.

2026-05-21_155929.webp.description: Yala Snow Moutain in the distance, clouds are gathering.

2026-05-22_133501.webp.description: Yajiang's spiral overpass, 300m vertical drop in just 8km distance (almost got scraped by a lorry here).

2026-05-23_112241.webp.description: 3000km road sign of G318, filled with messages from cyclists. This stretch is the most steep 10km of the journey, averaging more 9-10% gradient.

2026-05-23_205337.webp.description: Three Sisters Hostel at Xiangkezong, a well-known pit stop for cyclists, motorcyclists, and backpackers. Its walls are filled with messages left by travellers.

2026-05-24_114951.webp.description: Me after climbing up The Eighteen Bends of the Sky Road.

2026-05-25_130524.webp.description: Yak sign on the way to Litang Tunnel.

2026-05-25_192000.webp.description: Changqingchun Ke'er Monastery under the afternoon sun.

2026-05-27_080411.webp.description: Messaged left behind by travellers on the wall of a hostel in Henixiang.

2026-05-27_122100.webp.description: Fellow cyclist near the top of Haizi Mountain, 4685m above sea level.

2026-05-21_125301.webp.description: Grassland from Xinduqiao to Tagong, a 80km recovery ride. I was assessing if I can still continue the journey after my injury.

2026-05-21_142801.webp.description: Buddhist murals on rocks near Tagong.
